trust_decision.summary: Header text taken from a peer-supplied SIP message is trusted to fit the fixed static buffer last_header[MAX_HEADER_LEN*10]; get_header() appends name, separators and content with unbounded sprintf, and nothing checks the size.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'oversized SIP header content'. The only generic header extractor is get_header()/get_header_content() in the mini SIP parser, and it writes into the static last_header buffer.

fix_sites.entry_point: received SIP message -> call::get_last_header() ([last_*] scenario keyword, content=false), src/call.cpp:1675 / src/call.cpp:4049
received SIP message with repeated headers (e.g. Via) -> get_header() concatenation; reached from call::process_incoming src/call.cpp:4655, src/call.cpp:5589
same as above (', ' separator between repeated headers)

received SIP message -> get_header_content() from call::process_incoming (src/call.cpp:5589, src/call.cpp:5602), call::extract_transaction (src/call.cpp:4433), socket trace (src/socket.cpp:1128), scenario Content-Length (src/scenario.cpp:852)
truncated: label, the shared exit after truncation (not a separate route)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published fix sites are in one function, get_header() in src/sip_parser.cpp:121-265. No second module is touched.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names get_header()'s last_header buffer. extract_transaction/extract_cseq_method in call.cpp copy into caller-owned buffers in another file, and get_first_line() handles the request/status line, not a 'header', and only runs under the -trace_shortmsg logging option. A solver can argue all of these are other buffers or features.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: get_header() must keep concatenating repeated headers (multiple Via / Record-Route, multiline folding) into one value, with name prefix when content=false. A fix that caps output at MAX_HEADER_LEN, returns empty on overflow, or stops after the first header breaks the [last_Via:] keyword and route-set computation. Callers (rr/contact/auth) already truncate with strncat to MAX_HEADER_LEN-1 and expect a non-empty prefix.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/sip_parser.cpp:201-218; src/sip_parser.cpp:656-670 (existing concatenation tests); src/call.cpp:5589-5590; src/call.cpp:5602-5604

O6_input_shapes: many repeated headers whose concatenation exceeds the buffer (separator writes)
content=false path that prefixes the header name
compact header forms (v:, i:, m:, f:, t: ...) matched via internal_compact_header_name
folded multiline headers (continuation lines with space/tab)

O7_producer.where: Data comes straight from the received network message (src/socket.cpp:474 bufrcv[SIPP_MAX_MSG_SIZE]); there is no schema, serializer or cache between them.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: call::extract_transaction copies the Via branch from get_header_content() (up to ~20 KB) into txn[MAX_HEADER_LEN] with no bound; reached for every received response
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different function, different file, and the caller owns the buffer. After the get_header fix the source is 'already truncated', but only to 20490 bytes, not 2049.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/call.cpp, a different file from the landing point; caller at src/call.cpp:5326, buffer at src/call.cpp:4613

O8_uncovered_routes.route: call::extract_cseq_method copies the CSeq method up to CR/LF from the raw message into responsecseqmethod[65] with no bound
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Does not go through get_header() at all and parses the raw message with strstr. It reads as a separate CSeq helper, not 'header content' extraction.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/call.cpp, a different file; buffer at src/call.cpp:4612, caller at src/call.cpp:5325

O8_uncovered_routes.route: get_first_line copies the start line into a static last_header[MAX_HEADER_LEN*10] with no index bound; a received message can be up to SIPP_MAX_MSG_SIZE (65536)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Start line, not a header. It is reached only via the -trace_shortmsg logging option (src/socket.cpp:1128, src/socket.cpp:2223).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, sibling function sharing the same buffer size

O8b_injection_room.sibling: get_header_field_code could copy the header content (not just the int) into static code[MAX_HEADER_LEN] with sprintf
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already uses an unbounded sprintf into a fixed static buffer, right next to get_header_content().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the [last_*] keyword expansion already does an unbounded sprintf of get_last_header() output into msg_buffer; a header-copy helper writing into a fixed local could sit here
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same idiom (dest += sprintf(dest, "%s", ...)) is used throughout createSendingMessage.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a get_call_id-style extractor for another header (e.g. Contact URI) that omits the length check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_call_id has an explicit length check. A copied helper that drops it is a plausible maintainer slip.

O9_family: memory-safety: fixed-size buffer overflow (CWE-120) on attacker-controlled SIP header text

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + g++; needs OpenSSL (or wolfSSL), ncurses/tinfo, pkg-config. PCAP/SCTP are optional. Unit tests need GoogleTest: the gtest submodule is not populated at the pinned tree, so system libgtest-dev is required (CMakeLists.txt:283-313).
O10_build.project_tests: gtest unit tests are compiled into sipp_unittest with -DGTEST and are embedded at the bottom of src/sip_parser.cpp (src/sip_parser.cpp:550 onward, get_header tests at src/sip_parser.cpp:656-680). There is also a shell regression suite in regress/runtests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the sprintf calls in get_header() with snprintf bounded by the remaining buffer and stop there. That leaves extract_transaction/extract_cseq_method in call.cpp and get_first_line open.

out_of_scope_notes: createSendingMessage expands [last_message] / [last_*] with unbounded sprintf into msg_buffer[SIPP_MAX_MSG_SIZE+2] (src/call.cpp:4051, src/call.cpp:4064). That is a different sink, not pursued.
